title: GitHub Copilot app

signIn.hint: The app's own frontend, read out of the installed app and run in a browser StuntDouble owns, connected to the app's local backend read-only (spike C). The app must be running and signed in.

errorPage.note: The app's error page (a native call the stand-in didn't answer): the capture fails instead of saving it.

fallbacks: Avatars and repository images keep their colors

platform.note: Window chrome after the fact: Mac traffic lights, or a Windows title bar (app icon and name, minimize, maximize, close). The header's own controls move to where the Windows build puts them (platforms/windows.json).

labels: aria-label of the user menu (it holds the account's name)
privacy.note: Personal labels never go in a pack: the platform pack keeps only the window controls' names and positions.

writes.what: Sends the prompt: a new session (or a new turn), and the agent runs
writes.note: Captures don't send prompts: the read-only stand-in answers every write itself, and a run is recorded from the real app's events instead (spike C, option c). Allowing a narrow set of writes needs the presenter's go-ahead and lives only in a private pack.

check.expect: No new session from the capture.

effects.what: Opening a session marks it read in the real app

check.expect: The capture drops read-state writes, so the app's unread dots stay as they were.

notes: The frontend is embedded in the app's binary (Tauri) and served at tauri.localhost; on Windows the same Tauri build embeds it the same way (WebView2). Which backend messages are reads, and the defaults a stand-in gives for native calls, name the app's internal message types: they live only in a private pack (~/.stuntdouble/packs/github-copilot-app), versioned per app build.
sources: spike C (Copilot app capture): match, error page, read-only capture, recorded events
spike A and B: themes, Windows platform pack
